config.documentTitleFull: MOTION FOR ORDER EXPUNGING THE RECORD OF CONVICTION (FIRST-TIME PROPERTY OFFENDER) PURSUANT TO HRS § 706-622.9, WITH DECLARATION UNDER HAW. R. PENAL P. 47(d)
config.courtCaption: IN THE [COURT THAT ENTERED THE JUDGMENT — CONFIRM THE COURT NAME FROM THE COURT RECORD], STATE OF HAWAII

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Conviction expungement for a first-time property offender. The grant is mandatory once the statutory findings are made — 'shall issue ... provided that (a) through (d)' — but two of the four provisos are findings the court makes, so the outcome is not mechanical; where the court cannot make the paragraph (b) finding it may nevertheless order expungement on finding successful completion of a substance abuse treatment program. This relief must not be described as automatic.

'An application to the court for an order shall be by motion' — the stage-one vehicle is a written motion in the participant's own existing penal case, filed in the court that sentenced or convicted them; the Rules of Penal Procedure govern because Rule 54(a) applies them to all penal proceedings.

verificationStatute.description: Rule 47(d) permits an unsworn declaration in lieu of an affidavit, subscribed as true under penalty of law and dated, which removes any notarization requirement from the stage-one filing.

config.serviceNote: Haw. R. Penal P. 49(a): all written submissions to the court shall be served upon each of the parties promptly after filing. The prosecuting attorney is a party to the underlying penal case and is served under that rule. Proof of service is required by Haw. R. Penal P. 49(c), so a certificate of service is part of the stage-one filing.
counselFlags: Packet copy must not describe subsection (4) relief as automatic: two of the four provisos are court findings, and the substance-abuse-treatment fallback is the only discretionary grant among the five stage-one statutes.
The sentencing date decides which subsection applies; the participant reads the case number and sentencing date from their own court record — LegalEase does not obtain or review the court record.

Stage two (HCJDC 159(b) Expungement Application to the Hawaii Criminal Justice Data Center, with a copy of the signed order attached) is an official form outside this packet: do not submit stage two until the court signs the stage-one order. An HCJDC application fee applies at stage two.

No fee is prescribed by the statute for the stage-one motion and the Judiciary publishes no filing fee for a motion filed in an existing penal case; clerk cost practice remains a release-level open question — confirm with the clerk.
No fee-waiver form is part of this packet: Haw. R. Penal P. Form B is the companion to the Rule 40 post-conviction petition, not an expungement component.
No statutory notice requirement exists; the only notice is Rule 49 service of the filed motion on the parties, including the prosecuting attorney.
Venue follows the offence and is a participant input, not a track constant; the caption's court name must be confirmed from the participant's own court record.

Self-help stop conditions: any prior or subsequent felony conviction in any jurisdiction; a contested nonviolence finding under subsection (4)(d); the discretionary substance-abuse fallback in play; prosecutor opposition or a contested hearing; any immigration matter.
The pinned registry records that nothing in the source makes the Hawaii implementation runtime-ready; this packet is build output for review, not live routing.

provenance.registryExcerpt: Two stages, both settled. Stage one is a written motion in the participant's own existing penal case, filed in the court that sentenced or convicted them, seeking a court order expunging the record of conviction; stage two is the HCJDC 159(b) Expungement Application submitted to the Hawaii Criminal Justice Data Center with a copy of that order attached. The stage-one vehicle is fixed by Haw. R. Penal P. 47(a) ('An application to the court for an order shall be by motion'); Rule 54(a) applies the Rules of Penal Procedure to all penal proceedings. Subsection (4) is mandatory once the findings are made — 'shall issue ... provided that (a) through (d)' — but two of the four are findings the court makes; where the court cannot make the paragraph (b) finding it 'may nevertheless' order expungement on finding successful completion of a substance abuse treatment programme; the packet copy must not describe subsection (4) relief as automatic. No official statewide Hawaii Judiciary expungement form exists for stage one in any circuit, so a controlled custom pleading is permitted and is the only available strategy. Venue follows the offence and is a participant input. Service: Haw. R. Penal P. 49(a) service on each party (the prosecuting attorney is a party), proof of service required by Haw. R. Penal P. 49(c). Verification: Haw. R. Penal P. 47(d) unsworn declaration in lieu of affidavit, subscribed as true under penalty of law and dated; no notarization. Fees: none prescribed for stage one; clerk cost practice is a release-level open question; an HCJDC application fee applies at stage two. Fee waiver: Haw. R. Penal P. Form B is not a component of an expungement packet.
